nodes.statement: Consider the distribution of z_L-1 under the prior. Let k be the covariance function of the NNGP associated to tfrac1sqrtMlrabmupvarepsilon, phi(z_L-1) + Z as M to infty, where bmupvarepsilon is a vector with i.i.d.\ N(0, 1) entries and Z sim N(0, 1). Henceforth, denote k(x) = k(x, x). Note that phi' = phisse' + phisso' = phisso' is an even function. Suppose that x mapsto E_P[phi'(sqrtk(x) Z)] is a constant function. By crefprop:convergence-lambda,prop:kernel-diagonal in combination with the assumed conditions on phi, it follows that k(R^Dssi) contains an open interval. Therefore, since phi' is a continuous even function and x mapsto E_P[phi'(sqrtk(x) Z)] is a constant function, by an argument similar to the proof of creflem:odd-fn1, phi' must be equal to a constant function. However, since phisso is non-linear, phi' = phisso' cannot be equal to a constant function. We conclude that x mapsto E_P[phi'(sqrtk(x) Z)] cannot be equal to a constant function: there exist two inputs x, x' in R^Dssi such that E_P[phi'(sqrtk(x) Z)] neq E_P[phi'(sqrtk(x') Z)]. Let c > 0 be the constant c = absE_P[phi'(sqrtk(x) Z)] - E_P[phi'(sqrtk(x') Z)]. Let K > 0. Consider the sequence of mean-field distributions (ensuremathQ_M)_M ge 1 constructed by setting everything equal to the prior except for E_Q_M[b_L]= mu 1 and E_ensuremathQ_M[W_L+1] = mu 1^T with mu = sqrtK/M. Then indeed KL(Q_M, P) = K. Moreover, tfrac1sqrtMW_L+1 phi(tfrac1sqrtMW_L phi(z_L-1) + b_L) + b_L+1 oversetd= tfrac1sqrtMlramu 1 + bmupvarepsilon, phi(tfrac1sqrtMmathbfcalE phi(z_L-1) + mu 1 + bmupvarepsilon') + bmupvarepsilon'' where bmupvarepsilon, bmupvarepsilon', bmupvarepsilon'', and mathbfcalE are respectively three vectors and a matrix with i.i.d.\ N(0,1) entries and where z_L is distributed under the prior. Using the observation that the elements of z_L are identically distributed, compute E_Q_M[f(x)] = tfracmusqrtM E_P[lra1, phi(tfrac1sqrtMmathbfcalE phi(z_L-1) + mu 1 + bmupvarepsilon')] = sqrtM mu\, E_P[phi(tfrac1sqrtMlrabmupvarepsilon''', phi(z_L-1) + Z + mu)] where bmupvarepsilon''' is a vector with i.i.d.\ N(0, 1) entries and Z sim N(0, 1). Note that sqrtMmu = sqrtK and call Y_M = tfrac1sqrtMlrabmupvarepsilon''', phi(z_L-1) + Z. From Theorem 4 by citetmatthews_2018 in combination with the assumed conditions on phi, it follows that Y_M smashotod sqrtk(x) Z where k is the earlier defined covariance function of the corresponding NNGP. We finally establish the asymptotic behaviour of E_Q_M[f(x)] - E_Q_M[f(x')] in two steps. First, by a second-order Taylor expansion of mu mapsto E_P[phi(Y_M + mu)] around mu = 0, using (a) normphi' < infty and normphi''_infty < infty to interchange derivative and expectation and (b) normphi''_infty < infty and mu^2 = o(tfrac1sqrtM) to determine the order of the error term, E_Q_M[f(x)] = sqrtK Big[ E_P[phi(Y_M)] + mu \,E_P[phi'(Y_M)] + o(tfrac1sqrtM) Big]. Note that Y_M oversetd= -Y_M, so E_P[phi(Y_M)] = phisse + E_P[phisso(Y_M)] = phisse. Second, since Y_M smashotod sqrtk(x) Z and phi' is continuous and bounded, E_P[phi'(Y_M)] to E_P[phi'(sqrtk(x) Z)]. Therefore, E_Q_M[f(x)] = sqrtK Big[ phisse + mu Big(E_P[phi'(sqrtk(x) Z)] + o(1) Big) + o(tfrac1sqrtM) Big], so, again using that sqrtM mu = sqrtK, sqrtM (E_Q_M[f(x)] - E_Q_M[f(x')]) = K Big(E_P[phi'(sqrtk(x) Z)] - E_P[phi'(sqrtk(x') Z)] + o(1) Big) + o(1) = c K + o(1), which concludes the proof.
nodes.raw_latex:
Consider the distribution of $\mathbf{z}_{L-1}$ under the prior.
    Let $k$ be the covariance function of the NNGP associated to $\tfrac1{\sqrt{M}}\lra{\bm{\upvarepsilon}, \phi(\mathbf{z}_{L-1})} + Z$ as $M \to \infty$, where $\bm{\upvarepsilon}$ is a vector with i.i.d.\ $\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ entries and $Z \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$.
    Henceforth, denote $k(\mathbf{x}) = k(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{x})$.

    Note that $\phi' = \phi\ss{e}' + \phi\ss{o}' = \phi\ss{o}'$ is an even function.
    Suppose that $\mathbf{x} \mapsto \mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi'(\sqrt{k(\mathbf{x})} Z)]$ is a constant function.
    By \cref{prop:convergence-lambda,prop:kernel-diagonal} in combination with the assumed conditions on $\phi$, it follows that $k(\mathbb{R}^{D\ss{i}})$ contains an open interval.
    Therefore, since $\phi'$ is a continuous even function and $\mathbf{x} \mapsto \mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi'(\sqrt{k(\mathbf{x})} Z)]$ is a constant function, by an argument similar to the proof of \cref{lem:odd-fn1}, $\phi'$ must be equal to a constant function.
    However, since $\phi\ss{o}$ is non-linear, $\phi' = \phi\ss{o}'$ cannot be equal to a constant function.
    We conclude that $\mathbf{x} \mapsto \mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi'(\sqrt{k(\mathbf{x})} Z)]$ cannot be equal to a constant function: there exist two inputs $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{x}' \in \mathbb{R}^{D\ss{i}}$ such that $\mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi'(\sqrt{k(\mathbf{x})} Z)] \neq \mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi'(\sqrt{k(\mathbf{x}')} Z)]$.
    Let $c > 0$ be the constant $c = \abs{\mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi'(\sqrt{k(\mathbf{x})} Z)] - \mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi'(\sqrt{k(\mathbf{x}')} Z)]}.$

    Let $K > 0$.
    Consider the sequence of mean-field distributions $(\ensuremath{Q}_M)_{M \ge 1}$ constructed by setting everything equal to the prior except for $\mathbb{E}_{Q_M}[\mathbf{b}_L]= \mu \mathbf{1}$ and $\mathbb{E}_{\ensuremath{Q}_M}[\mathbf{W}_{L+1}] = \mu \mathbf{1}^{\text{\textsf{T}}}$ with $\mu = \sqrt{K/M}$.
    Then indeed $\operatorname{KL}(Q_M, P) = K$.
    Moreover,
    \begin{equation}
        \tfrac1{\sqrt{M}}\mathbf{W}_{L+1} \phi(\tfrac1{\sqrt{M}}\mathbf{W}_L \phi(\mathbf{z}_{L-1}) + \mathbf{b}_L) + \mathbf{b}_{L+1}
        \overset{\text{d}}{=}
        \tfrac1{\sqrt{M}}\lra{\mu \mathbf{1} + \bm{\upvarepsilon}, \phi(\tfrac1{\sqrt{M}}\mathbfcal{E} \phi(\mathbf{z}_{L-1}) + \mu \mathbf{1} + \bm{\upvarepsilon}')} + \bm{\upvarepsilon}''
    \end{equation}
    where $\bm{\upvarepsilon}$, $\bm{\upvarepsilon}'$, $\bm{\upvarepsilon}''$, and $\mathbfcal{E}$ are respectively three vectors and a matrix with i.i.d.\ $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ entries and where $\mathbf{z}_L$ is distributed under the prior.
    Using the observation that the elements of $\mathbf{z}_L$ are identically distributed, compute
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbb{E}_{Q_M}[f(\mathbf{x})] = \tfrac\mu{\sqrt{M}} \mathbb{E}_{P}[\lra{\mathbf{1}, \phi(\tfrac1{\sqrt{M}}\mathbfcal{E} \phi(\mathbf{z}_{L-1}) + \mu \mathbf{1} + \bm{\upvarepsilon}')}]
        = \sqrt{M} \mu\, \mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi(\tfrac1{\sqrt{M}}\lra{\bm{\upvarepsilon}''', \phi(\mathbf{z}_{L-1})} + Z + \mu)]
        
    \end{equation}
    where $\bm{\upvarepsilon}'''$ is a vector with i.i.d.\ $\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ entries and $Z \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$.
    Note that $\sqrt{M}\mu = \sqrt{K}$ and
    call $Y_M = \tfrac1{\sqrt{M}}\lra{\bm{\upvarepsilon}''', \phi(\mathbf{z}_{L-1})} + Z$.
    From Theorem 4 by \citet{matthews_2018} in combination with the assumed conditions on $\phi$, it follows that $Y_M \smash{\oto{\text{d}} \sqrt{k(\mathbf{x})}} Z$ where $k$ is the earlier defined covariance function of the corresponding NNGP.
    
    We finally establish the asymptotic behaviour of $\mathbb{E}_{Q_M}[f(\mathbf{x})] - \mathbb{E}_{Q_M}[f(\mathbf{x}')]$ in two steps.
    First, by a second-order Taylor expansion of $\mu \mapsto \mathbb{E}_P[\phi(Y_M + \mu)]$ around $\mu = 0$, using (a) $\norm{\phi'} < \infty $ and $\norm{\phi''}_\infty < \infty$ to interchange derivative and expectation and (b) $\norm{\phi''}_\infty < \infty$ and $\mu^2 = o(\tfrac1{\sqrt{M}})$ to determine the order of the error term,
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbb{E}_{Q_M}[f(\mathbf{x})] 
        = \sqrt{K} \Big[
            \mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi(Y_M)]
            + \mu \,\mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi'(Y_M)]
            + o(\tfrac1{\sqrt{M}})
        \Big].
    \end{equation}
    Note that $Y_M \overset{\text{d}}{=} -Y_M$, so $\mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi(Y_M)] = \phi\ss{e} + \mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi\ss{o}(Y_M)] = \phi\ss{e}$.
    Second, since $Y_M \smash{\oto{\text{d}} \sqrt{k(\mathbf{x})}} Z$ and $\phi'$ is continuous and bounded, $\mathbb{E}_P[\phi'(Y_M)] \to \mathbb{E}_P[\phi'(\sqrt{k(\mathbf{x})} Z)]$.
    Therefore,
    \begin{equation}
         \mathbb{E}_{Q_M}[f(\mathbf{x})] 
        = \sqrt{K} \Big[
            \phi\ss{e}
            + \mu \Big(\mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi'(\sqrt{k(\mathbf{x})} Z)] + o(1) \Big)
            + o(\tfrac1{\sqrt{M}})
        \Big],
    \end{equation}
    so, again using that $\sqrt{M} \mu = \sqrt{K}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \sqrt{M}
        (\mathbb{E}_{Q_M}[f(\mathbf{x})] 
        - \mathbb{E}_{Q_M}[f(\mathbf{x}')])
        =
            K \Big(\mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi'(\sqrt{k(\mathbf{x})} Z)] - \mathbb{E}_{P}[\phi'(\sqrt{k(\mathbf{x}')} Z)] + o(1) \Big)
            + o(1)
        = c K + o(1),
    \end{equation}
    which concludes the proof.
